edits.current:
The [closed value-index archive](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-perl-promotion-20261020.md)
adds top-level copied records indexed by closed `Bool`, `String`, and `Nat`
values. The index remains authenticated Lean metadata rather than a Perl field;
`Math::BigInt` carries every Nat payload field.

[Perl closed value-index checked records](checked-record-value-index-perl-promotion-20261020.md)
record four hosted CPAN selections across four interpreter ABIs and both
prebuilt-only and build-XS delivery modes for top-level copied checked-record
parameter/result sites with closed Bool, String, and Nat indices.

edits.previous: The compiler and reviewed contract admit three canonical index kinds: an unbounded `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String`. They are serialized as unsigned decimal, `true`/`false`, and exact Unicode-scalar text respectively; zero, the empty string, and supplementary characters are valid. Lean reduces a closed expression before recording it, so `1 + 2` and `decide (1 < 2)` become `3` and `true`. Open or opaque values are rejected. `Int`, `Char`, fixed-width or platform-width integers, `Fin`, functions, proofs, instances, and other index types require a separately reviewed representation and are not inferred from a host value. The [native-PHP value-index archive](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-php-promotion-20261019.md) exercises all three closed forms at top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites; the broader installed rollout remains separately tracked.

edits.previous: For a record whose proofs relate its fields, use a [checked constructor over the payload fields](existing-package.md#export-a-record-with-proof-fields). The host supplies no proof. The compiler checks each input through the selected Lean constructor and erases proofs from Lean-produced results. Closed `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String` indices stay in authenticated type metadata and never become host fields; the [native-PHP value-index archive](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-php-promotion-20261019.md) exercises all three closed forms at top-level copied checked-record sites. Top-level inputs and results have installed acceptance in C/C++, Node JavaScript/TypeScript, browser pages, React, workers, Python, Rust, Ruby, .NET, Java/Kotlin, Perl, native PHP, PHP-Wasm and WIT/WASI. npm has [installed nested acceptance](../evidence/nested-checked-record-browser-20261016/index.json), C/C++ have an [installed nested archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-native-20261016/index.json), .NET has an [installed NuGet archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-dotnet-20261016/index.json), Java/Kotlin have an [installed Maven archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-jvm-20261016/index.json), Perl has an [installed CPAN archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-perl-20261016/index.json), native PHP has an [installed Composer archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-20261016/index.json), Python has an [installed wheel archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-python-20261016/index.json), Ruby has an [installed gem archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-ruby-20261016/index.json), WIT/WASI has an [installed component archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-wit-20261016/index.json), PHP-Wasm has an [installed Node/Chromium archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-wasm-20261016/index.json), and Rust has an [installed Cargo archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-rust-20261016/index.json). They cover direct and repeated parameters, arrays, lists, options, products, `Except`/`Result`, enclosing record fields, active variant fields and constructor-free container results. [Installed inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) additionally covers the tested acyclic `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain, with independently selected parent and child constructors and proof-free results. Select the record constructor and each nested checked field's constructor independently at every public input site; only an active variant branch runs. Generic or recursive checked records, value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, callback, owned and open dependent combinations remain unfinished.

Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call."
